shortDescription: Manage SSH roles in HashiCorp Vault

options.name: algorithm_signer
options.description: Algorithm to use when signing certificates. Note that the default of C(rsa-sha2-512) is different from the upstream default, which is C(ssh-rsa) for historical reasons.

options.name: allow_bare_domains
options.description: Allows this role to sign host certificates for the domains specified in I(allowed_domains).

options.name: allow_host_certificates
options.description: Allows this role to sign host certificates. Either this or I(allow_user_certificates) must be C(true) when I(state=present).

options.name: allow_subdomains
options.description: Allows this role to sign host certificates for subdomains of the domains specified in I(allowed_domains).

options.name: allow_user_certificates
options.description: Allows this role to sign user certificates. Either this or I(allow_host_certificates) must be C(true) when I(state=present).

options.name: allow_user_key_ids
options.description: Allow signing requests to override the automatically generated key ID.

options.name: allowed_critical_options
options.description: Critical options a certificate can have when signed. An empty list allows all options.

options.name: allowed_domains
options.description: Domains for which this role can sign keys.

options.name: allowed_extensions
options.description: Extensions a certificate can have when signed. An empty list allows all extensions.

options.name: allowed_user_key_lengths
options.description: Mapping of SSH key types and their allowed sizes.

options.name: allowed_users
options.description: Users for which this role can sign keys. Defaults to I(default_user) if this is not set and I(default_user) is.

options.name: client_cert
options.description: PEM formatted certificate chain file to be used for TLS client authentication. This file can also include the key as well, and if the key is included, C(client_key) is not required.

options.name: client_key
options.description: PEM formatted file that contains your private key to be used for TLS client authentication. If C(client_cert) contains both the certificate and key, this option is not required.

options.name: default_critical_options
options.description: Options applied if none are provided in the signing request.

options.name: default_extensions
options.description: Extensions applied if none are provided in the signing request.

options.name: default_user
options.description: Default user to sign keys for.

options.name: http_agent
options.description: Header to identify as, generally appears in web server logs.

options.name: key_id_format
options.description: Custom format for automatically generated key IDs. Vault allows the variables C({{token_display_name}}), C({{role_name}}), and C({{public_key_hash}}) to be used.

options.name: max_ttl
options.description: Maximum length of time a certificate can be valid, in seconds. C(0) will use the system default.

options.name: mount_point
options.description: Path where the backend is mounted.

options.name: name
options.description: Name of the role to manage.

options.name: not_before_duration
options.description: Amount to backdate the ValidAfter property, in seconds.

options.name: state
options.description: Desired state of the role.

options.name: timeout
options.description: Request timeout, in seconds.

options.name: token
options.description: Authentication token to use. If this is not set then the contents of C(~/.vault-token) will be checked.

options.name: ttl
options.description: Default length of time the certificate will be valid, in seconds. C(0) will use the system default.

options.name: use_proxy
options.description: If C(no), it will not use a proxy, even if one is defined in an environment variable on the target hosts.

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: If C(no), TLS certificates will not be validated. This should only be used on personally controlled sites using self-signed certificates.

options.name: vault_addr
options.description: Location of the Vault service.
